summary: On 3 February 2020 around 8:30 a.m. ET Microsoft Teams became unavailable. Microsoft said an authentication certificate had expired and that it was developing a fix to apply a new certificate.

overview.background: Teams depends on authentication certificates for its service. When one expires and is not renewed, services needing it fail.
overview.impact: Users could not access Teams. The article gives no end time.
overview.severity: A public outage that lasted for hours (the card says several hours).
overview.gaps: This file uses a TechCrunch report. Microsoft's status history (the card source) could not be read.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: An unrenewed certificate stops sign-in
diagrams.caption: Per Microsoft's statement, an authentication certificate expired and users had issues using the service.

nodes.label: Users cannot sign in or use Teams

diagrams.title: Certificate inventory and expiry alerts (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: General controls: track every certificate, alert early and automate renewal.

afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: An authentication certificate reaches its expiry without being renewed.
Microsoft says an authentication certificate has expired.
Microsoft develops and begins to deploy a new certificate.

rootCause.trigger: An authentication certificate expired and had not been renewed.
rootCause.underlying: Services that needed the certificate failed.

evidence.label: Microsoft's statement
evidence.body: We've determined that an authentication certificate has expired causing, users to have issues using the service.
evidence.note: From Microsoft as quoted by TechCrunch.

evidence.label: The fix
evidence.body: developing a fix to apply a new certificate to the service

diagnose.step: Read the TLS or token errors.
Check expiry dates of auth certificates.

correct.step: Issue and deploy a new certificate.

verify.step: Check other certificates for upcoming expiry.

fix.safety: Replace certificates in a controlled order. A bad replacement can cause a second outage.

troubleshoot.scenario: Sign-ins fail and logs show an authentication certificate has expired.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
hints: How do you prevent a repeat?
troubleshoot.answer: Issue and deploy a new certificate, sweep for others near expiry and automate renewal with alerts.

design.prompt: Design certificate management for a global service.
design.answer: Central inventory, owner per certificate, automatic renewal, alerts and drills.
